artboards.title: Today — what it looks like now

annotations.text:
TODAY

The Project tab, recreated from index.html and style.css at the values actually in the file.

What dates it: raw browser controls (the whole control styling is `padding: 4px 6px`), a grey #f7f7f7 chrome bar, uppercase letter-spaced grey headings on hairline underlines, and everything separated by a 1px line rather than by space.

No accent colour exists anywhere. Delete looks exactly like New project.

OPTION 1 — RESKIN

Same structure, same section order, same table columns, same header contents. Only the skin changes: design tokens, styled controls, one indigo accent, cards and space instead of hairlines, sentence-case headings, and a real button hierarchy (primary / secondary / ghost).

WHY: most of the visual gain for almost none of the risk — no geometry is touched, so no chart can break.

TRADEOFF: the information architecture is untouched. The header is still eight controls in one row, and Export/Import still sit at navigation weight.

OPTION 2 — RESKIN + SHELL REBUILD

Option 1's skin, plus a rebuilt shell: a sidebar takes navigation AND the project list (so the picker becomes a filterable list with real status dots and tier digits, instead of a native <select> carrying emoji). A top bar names what you are looking at and carries its actions. Warnings move to the top. Goal and Details sit side by side. Export/Import are demoted to the sidebar foot.

WHY: this is where ease of use actually comes from — the header stops being a junk drawer.

TRADEOFF: it edits index.html structure, so `node scripts/wire_check.js` becomes mandatory, and --topbar-h (published, read by .sprint-scope) has to move with it.

NOTE: charts are untouched in BOTH options — same bar colours, same week grid, same metrics. Restyling those is Option 3, still undecided.
